errors.description: The claimed swap-dependent nonlocality cannot follow from the stated criterion. Swapping the qubits changes the correlation matrix from β to βᵀ, but βᵀβ and ββᵀ have the same eigenvalues, so M is unchanged. In the stated row- or column-supported cases, both give eigenvalues (‖b‖², 0, 0); consequently Eq. (9) cannot make one labelling nonlocal and the swapped labelling local.
errors.evidence: Definition 1.2 interchanges the Pauli factors, which transposes the correlation coefficients. Equation (3) uses the two largest eigenvalues of βᵀβ, while Eq. (8) asserts an asymmetry between the row- and column-supported cases.

errors.location: Eqs. (6)–(7); construction in the proof of Theorem 1.4
errors.description: The eigenvalue formulas omit the overall factor 1/4 from the definition of ρ. For example, when all coefficients vanish, Eq. (7) gives four eigenvalues equal to 1, although Eq. (1) gives ρ = I₄/4, whose eigenvalues are 1/4. As a result, the construction's stated distance excess |λ₀| gives an actual minimum eigenvalue −|λ₀|/4, not λ₀.
errors.evidence: Equation (1) defines ρ with prefactor 1/4, but Eqs. (6)–(7) list eigenvalues without that prefactor; Theorem 1.4 identifies λ₀ as the smallest eigenvalue of ρ.

errors.location: Theorem 1.1 and its use of “nonlocal” and “local”
errors.description: The condition in Eq. (3) tests violation of the CHSH inequality, not Bell nonlocality in the unrestricted sense used elsewhere in the manuscript. Failure to violate CHSH does not, by itself, establish a local hidden-variable model for all Bell inequalities and measurements. Thus the stated “iff” and the corresponding general locality claims overreach unless “nonlocal” is restricted to CHSH nonlocality.
errors.evidence: The manuscript introduces an experimentally testable Bell inequality and then states that M > 1 is equivalent to nonlocality, without limiting the claim to violation of that inequality.
